4 9. My issue-wise findings are as under:-
ISSUE No.1:
Whether the deceased Touheed Alam Barvi @ Tohid died in road traffic accident on 13.10.2021 at about 10:10 PM at Outer Ring Road, EE Block Red Light Signal,
Jahangir Puri, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS. Jahangir Puri due to resh and negligent driving of vehicle bearing registration no. HR55V-5050 by its driver Sh.
Mukaddish/R-1, owned by Sh. Satpal Singh Chopra/R-2 and insured with United India Insurance Co. Ltd./R-3?

OPP Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners and to prove that victim suffered fatal injuries in this accident on account of rash and negligence on the part of respondent no. 1, petitioners examined PW3 HC Sanni Malik who deposed that on 13/14.10.2021, he was on the highway patrolling duty from 8 pm to 8 am.
At about 10.30 pm, he along with HC Ram Kishore were patrolling on two different bikes.

On reaching EE Block red light traffic signal, a truck bearing no. HR55V 5050 came from Madhuban Chowk side in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, a bike going ahead bearing registration no. DL5SBS 2959 (Hero Super Splender), Black colour was hit by the erring truck bearing no. HR55V 5050 and it dragged the motorcyclist for about 200 meters, as the shirt of the motorcyclist got struck in the front bumper of the truck he followed the truck and on reaching Mukundpur flyover, he apprehended the truck driver and HC Ram Kishore made a call on 100 number.
He specifically deposed that accident occurred due to high speed, rash and negligent driving by the erring truck bearing no. HR55V 5050 solely.
Though, PW3 has been duly Page no. 6 MACT No. 111/22 Digitally signed Rihana & Ors.

PW3 denied the suggestion that he was not present at the spot.
Nothing material has come on record in the cross examination of PW3.

PW2 has been cross examined by the respondent no.1 and 2 but neither respondent no.1 nor respondent no. 2 examined themselves particularly respondent no. 1 to prove that he has been falsely implicated in the present case or that PW3 is deposing falsely with regard to the involvement of vehicle in question or that respondent no. 1 has not caused any accident.

Further, the criminal case record filed along with the DAR, which is collectively Ex. PW1/3 shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/304A IPC.
Apart from deposition of PWs, the fact that victim suffered fatal injuries in the accident is also supported by his postmortem report filed along with DAR.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against his false implication in the present case.

sentences.text: "The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident "speaks for itself" or tell's its own story.
There are cases in which the accident speaks for itself so that it is sufficient for the plaintiff to prove the accident and nothing more.
It will then be for the defendant to establish that the accident happened due to some other cause than his own negligence.
Page no. 7 Rihana & Ors. Vs. Mukaddish & Ors.
SUNIL Digitally signed by SUNIL KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2025.07.09 16:12:42 +0530

Salmond on the Law of Torts (15th Ed.) at p. 306 states: "The maxim res ipsa loquitur applies whenever it is so improbable that such an accident would have happened without the negligence of the defendant that a reasonable jury could find without further evidence that it was so caused."

In Halsbury's Laws of England, 3rd Ed., Vol. 28, at p. 77, the position is stated thus: "An exception to the general rule that the burden of proof of the alleged negligence is in the first instance on the plaintiff occurs wherever the facts already established are such that the proper and natural inference arising from them is ,that the injury complained of was caused by the defendant's negligence, or where the event charged as negligence "tells its own story'
of negligence on the part of the defendant, the story so told being clear and unambiguous."

Further, relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under: -
"The plaintiff can prove the accident but cannot prove how it happened to establish negligence.

entities.text: Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This hardship is to be avoided by applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur.
The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident speaks for itself or tells its own story".
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".

Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and victim suffered fatal injuries in the said accident

The Issue no. 1 is accordingly decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents holding that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle in question by the respondent no. 1 and victim/ deceased suffered fatal injuries in the said accident.

Whether the LRs of deceased are entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?

OPP.
10.
As far as the issue with respect to right to claim compensation is concerned, there is no dispute that petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased.
Accordingly, petitioners i.e. widow, mother and minor sons and daughter are to be considered to be dependent upon the income of deceased.
Accordingly, the question of right of the petitioners for claiming of compensation is decided in favour of the petitioners.

Now, the second part of the issue in hand with respect to the quantum of compensation is to be adjudicated and below are the finding: -
11.
It is deposed by PW1 / widow of deceased that her deceased husband was skilled welder and earning Rs. 33,500/- per month.

Admittedly, no appointment letter, nor any salary slip, bank statement etc. has been filed to prove that deceased was earning such amount nor any witness has been examined in support of such contention nor any educational qualification document has been filed.
In such scenario, compensation amount towards monthly loss of dependency is to be computed on the basis of minimum wages of unskilled labour, which was Rs. 16,064/-.

Accordingly,
this amount of Rs. 16,064/- per month is taken for calculating the loss of future income.

12. As per adhar card of victim, his date of birth is 01.01.1985, which inter alia means that victim was more than 36 years in age as on the date of accident and as per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680 of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and future benefit has to be given @ 40% in case, the deceased was self employed and below the age of 40, at the time of accident.

Accordingly, the monthly income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.22,489.6p (16064 + 40% =
22,489.6)
13.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Date: 2025.07.09 16:12:27 +0530 140 of The Motor Vehicle's Act, 1988 (in short 'M.V. Act') seeking compensation from respondents on account of fatal injuries suffered by victim Touheed Alam Barvi (hereinafter referred to as 'victim / deceased) in road traffic accident occurred on 13.10.2021.
The offending truck HR-55V-5050 tried to fled from the spot of accident after hitting the motor cycle and kept on dragging the struck body of victim Touheed Alam Barmi for a considerable distance and was apprehended by police after some distance, which to which deceased suffered fatal injuries.
He was taken to BJRM Hospital however he was declared brought dead vide MLC No. 184927/21 by BJRM Hospital Delhi.
Further, the criminal case record filed along with the DAR, which is collectively Ex. PW1/3 shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/304A IPC.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the LRs of deceased are entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?
4 9. My issue-wise findings are as under:-
ISSUE No.1:
Whether the deceased Touheed Alam Barvi @ Tohid died in road traffic accident on 13.10.2021 at about 10:10 PM at Outer Ring Road, EE Block Red Light Signal,
Jahangir Puri, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS. Jahangir Puri due to resh and negligent driving of vehicle bearing registration no. HR55V-5050 by its driver Sh.
Mukaddish/R-1, owned by Sh. Satpal Singh Chopra/R-2 and insured with United India Insurance Co. Ltd./R-3?
It will then be for the defendant to establish that the accident happened due to some other cause than his own negligence.
The Issue no. 1 is accordingly decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents holding that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle in question by the respondent no. 1 and victim/ deceased suffered fatal injuries in the said accident.
Whether the LRs of deceased are entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against his false implication in the present case.
Relying upon judgment in Pushpabai Purshottam Rihana And Ors.
Udeshi & Ors vs Ranjit Ginning & Pressing Co. (P) Ltd. & Anr. 1977 (2) SCC 745 Civil Appeal No. 2071 of 1968, decided on March 25, 1977 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India wherein it was held as under: -
Page no. 7 Rihana & Ors. Vs. Mukaddish & Ors.
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".
Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and victim suffered fatal injuries in the said accident
As far as the issue with respect to right to claim compensation is concerned, there is no dispute that petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased.
In such scenario, compensation amount towards monthly loss of dependency is to be computed on the basis of minimum wages of unskilled labour, which was Rs. 16,064/-.
Accordingly,
this amount of Rs. 16,064/- per month is taken for calculating the loss of future income.
12. As per adhar card of victim, his date of birth is 01.01.1985, which inter alia means that victim was more than 36 years in age as on the date of accident and as per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680 of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and future benefit has to be given @ 40% in case, the deceased was self employed and below the age of 40, at the time of accident.
Accordingly, the monthly income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.22,489.6p (16064 + 40% =
22,489.6)
13.
To calculate future loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased, as per the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sarla Verma (Supra), which per which, the multiplier of 15 is applicable for the persons aged between 36-40 years in age.
All these facts show that there is negligence on the part of victim as well and thus contributory negligence is well found on the part of deceased also.
Relying upon the judgment in Santosh Kanwar and Ors Vs. Om Prakash & Ors. 1986 ACJ 799 wherein it was held as under: -
